items.q: Is intimacy over after menopause?
items.a: Not at all. Dryness and discomfort are treatable, and many people enjoy intimacy for decades after.

items.q: I’m a man of 55 with low energy. Is it testosterone?
items.a: Possibly, but sleep, weight, mood, diabetes and thyroid are common causes. See a doctor for proper tests before any treatment.

quiz.q: Menopause is confirmed after…
quiz.why: Menopause is confirmed after 12 months without periods. A hot flush or age 40 alone doesn't confirm it.

quiz.q: Any bleeding after menopause should…
options: Always be checked by a doctor
quiz.why: Any bleeding after menopause should always be checked by a doctor, because it can signal a serious condition. It is not to be ignored.

quiz.q: Which helps bone health after menopause?
options: Weight-bearing exercise with calcium and vitamin D
quiz.why: Weight-bearing exercise with calcium and vitamin D helps bone health after menopause. Smoking, caffeine and inactivity weaken bones.

quiz.q: Male testosterone with age usually…
quiz.why: Male testosterone usually declines gradually with age. It doesn't drop suddenly at 50 or stay the same.

quiz.q: Self-medicating with testosterone can…
quiz.why: Self-medicating with testosterone can cause infertility and other risks, because it suppresses the body's own production. Use only under a doctor.

lessons.title: The ageing body: what's normal, what's not

scenes.text: Mrs. Leela Pillai, 70, from Kochi leaks a little urine when she coughs and is too embarrassed to tell anyone.
Mr. Pillai, 73, gets up 3 times a night to urinate and thinks it’s ‘just age’.
Their granddaughter, a nurse, persuades them to see their doctor together.
Leela learns pelvic floor exercises; Mr. Pillai is treated for an enlarged prostate. They sleep better and go to their grandson’s wedding with confidence.

steps.title: Normal ageing
steps.body: Normal ageing includes: slower metabolism, some loss of muscle and bone, needing reading glasses, some hearing changes, drier skin, slightly slower memory recall, lighter sleep. Staying active slows many of these.

steps.title: Common but treatable — not ‘just age’
steps.body:
- **Urinary leakage** (incontinence) — pelvic floor exercises, treatment
- **Getting up often at night to urinate** — prostate, diabetes, heart or sleep causes
- **Hearing loss** — linked to isolation and cognitive decline; hearing aids help
- **Low mood** — depression is not a normal part of ageing
- **Memory problems that disrupt daily life** — get assessed
- **Falls** — check vision, medicines, balance, home safety
- **Constipation, sexual difficulties, joint pain** — all worth discussing

steps.title: Ageing well
steps.body:
- Move daily: walking, strength exercises twice a week, balance work (yoga, tai chi)
- Protein, fruits, vegetables, water
- Social connection and purpose
- Regular check-ups: BP, sugar, cholesterol, eyes, hearing, bones; recommended cancer screenings
- Vaccines advised for older adults (ask your doctor)
- Review medicines yearly to avoid harmful combinations

steps.title: Worked example: pelvic floor exercise
steps.body: Squeeze the muscles you’d use to stop passing urine or wind, hold for about 5 seconds, relax for 5 seconds; repeat 10 times, 3 times a day. Don’t hold your breath or tighten your tummy or thighs. Improvement often takes weeks to months; a physiotherapist can guide you. These help men too.

activity.prompt: Normal ageing, or worth seeing a doctor?

items.text: Needing reading glasses at 50
Leaking urine when coughing
Feeling hopeless for weeks
Slightly slower recall of names
Getting up 3–4 times a night to urinate
Getting lost on familiar routes
Drier skin

quiz.q: Is depression a normal part of ageing?
quiz.why: No, depression is not a normal part of ageing. It is treatable at any age.

quiz.q: Urinary leakage when coughing…
options: Often improves with pelvic floor exercises and treatment
quiz.why: Urinary leakage when coughing often improves with pelvic floor exercises and treatment. It isn't untreatable or just something to ignore.

quiz.q: Hearing loss in older adults is linked to…
quiz.why: Hearing loss in older adults is linked to isolation and cognitive decline. Hearing aids can help.

quiz.q: A pelvic floor squeeze should be held about…
quiz.why: A pelvic floor squeeze should be held for about 5 seconds, followed by 5 seconds rest. Repeating regularly strengthens the muscles.

quiz.q: Strength exercise is recommended…
quiz.why: WHO recommends strength exercise about twice a week, including for older adults. It isn't only for athletes.

lessons.title: Money shame: the secret nobody talks about

scenes.text: Vivek, 38, from Bengaluru has ₹6 lakh of credit card debt and a personal loan. His wife doesn’t know.
He can’t sleep, lies about expenses, and feels like a failure as a provider.
After a panic attack, he tells his wife. She’s upset — but relieved to know the truth.
Together they list all debts, make a plan, talk to the bank and a counsellor. Two years later, they’re debt-free.

steps.title: Why money brings shame
steps.body: Money is tied to identity, family expectations and status — ‘log kya kahenge’. People hide debt, salary, losses, or not being able to support parents. Shame leads to secrecy, which makes problems grow. Money stress is linked with anxiety, depression, relationship conflict and poor sleep.

steps.title: Step 1: see the whole picture
steps.body: List every debt: lender, amount, interest rate, minimum payment, due date. Write monthly income and essential expenses. Seeing numbers is scary but reduces anxiety — the unknown is worse.

steps.title: Worked example: avalanche vs snowball
steps.body:
Debts: credit card ₹2,00,000 at ~36% a year; personal loan ₹3,00,000 at 14%; friend ₹1,00,000 at 0%.
- **Avalanche:** pay minimums on all, put extra money on the **highest interest** (credit card) first — saves the most interest
- **Snowball:** pay off the **smallest** balance first for motivation

At 36% a year, ₹2 lakh costs about ₹6,000 in interest **per month** (2,00,000 × 0.36 ÷ 12) — so it’s usually first.

steps.title: Traps and scams
steps.body:
- Instant loan apps with hidden fees and harassment — use only RBI-regulated lenders; report harassment at **1930** / cybercrime.gov.in
- Borrowing from one card to pay another without a plan
- ‘Get rich quick’ trading or gaming schemes to ‘win back’ losses
- Hiding debt from a partner

steps.title: Talking about money
steps.body: With a partner: ‘I’ve been ashamed to tell you something about money. I want us to solve it together.’ Banks can sometimes restructure loans — ask. Free financial-literacy resources from RBI and SEBI explain basics. If stress is affecting your mood or sleep: **Tele-MANAS 14416**.

quiz.q: Why does money shame make problems worse?
quiz.why: Money shame makes problems worse because secrecy lets problems grow. Sharing and planning early helps.

quiz.q: Avalanche method pays first…
quiz.why: The avalanche method pays off the debt with the highest interest rate first, which saves the most interest. The smallest-balance method is the 'snowball'.

quiz.q: Instant loan app harassment can be reported at…
quiz.why: Instant loan app harassment can be reported at 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in, the cyber fraud reporting channels. 1098 is Childline and 1097 the AIDS helpline.

quiz.q: ₹2,00,000 at 36% per year costs about how much interest per month?
quiz.why: Monthly interest = principal × annual rate ÷ 12 = 2,00,000 × 0.36 ÷ 12 = ₹6,000.

quiz.q: A good first step?
options: List every debt with rate and due date
quiz.why: List every debt with its rate and due date, so you can see the whole picture and plan. Hiding statements, gambling or taking a new loan makes it worse.

questions.q: ED can be an early sign of…
questions.why: Erectile difficulty can be an early sign of heart disease, because both depend on healthy blood vessels. So it is worth getting checked, not a sign of good fitness.
Testosterone supplements can lower sperm production, because the body senses enough hormone and cuts its own signals to the testes. They don't boost fertility.

options: Benefits often outweigh risks — decide with a doctor
questions.why: For healthy women under 60 or within 10 years of menopause, the benefits of HRT often outweigh the risks, but the decision should be made with a doctor. It is not always dangerous.
Pregnancy is still possible in perimenopause, because ovulation can occur until menopause is confirmed (12 months without periods, over 50). So contraception may still be needed.
